Subject: Post-call: PII retention, marketplace subprocessors & telemetry follow-up

Anna — thanks for today’s demo and the time with your security team. Quick recap and a proposed set of next steps so we have alignment before the security deep-dive: 

Key points from call:
- You’ll send current data classification and where PII may appear (event payloads, user attributes, attachments).
- Marketplace flow: onboarding via your marketplace listing routes telemetry through a partner marketplace proxy — need clarity on which subprocessors see full event payloads.
- Retention: you mentioned default logs retained 90 days, backups longer; need explicit retention windows for any PII-derived artifacts.
- Logging/Access: who from vendor telemetry (EventLytics) can access raw events vs. aggregated telemetry?

Questions / asks for next steps (can you confirm these items by next Tue?):
1) Data classification CSV (columns: field, pii_flag, retention_days) — attach if possible.
2) Subprocessor list for marketplace flow (name, purpose, data types) and whether they are in-scope for DPA/SOC 2.
3) Which cloud region hosts event processing for marketplace customers (region + provider).
4) Any current mitigations for PII egress to analytics vendors (hashing, tokenization, prefix scrubbing).

Attachments: redwood-data-handling-summary.pdf (high level from our side) — I’ve attached a one-page we use internally so you know what we’ll need for our DPA review.

Proposed meeting: Security deep-dive with your eng/sec + EventLytics ops — 60m. Monica, can you lead the risk checklist on our side? Marissa, FYI for deal approvals/discount ask if needed.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez

Thanks, Sergio — great meeting. See inline answers below and attached CSV with our current classification.

Inline: 
1) Data classification: attached (cloudscale-data-classification.csv). PII primarily: email, name, billing_address, ssn_token (we tokenize ssn at ingestion).
2) Subprocessors: marketplace flow uses MarketProxy Inc. (proxying onboarding + billing) and EventLytics (telemetry ingestion & analytics). We’ve also got a logging provider (LogStream Ltd.) for aggregated logs. I’ve attached the draft marketplace contract showing subprocessors.
3) Cloud region: primary processing for EU marketplace customers is eu-west-1 (AWS).
4) Mitigations: 
   - Event payloads: we redact user-generated free-text on ingestion for marketplace flows unless customers opt-in.
   - SSN and other high-sensitivity fields are tokenized at collector.
   - EventLytics only receives event-level payloads for customers who enable deep-analytics; otherwise we send aggregated metrics.

Attachments included: cloudscale-data-classification.csv, marketplace-contract-draft.docx

Happy to set the security deep-dive. How does Wed 26 Aug 10:00 UTC look for your team and EventLytics ops (vendor-telemetry@eventlytics.io)?

Best,

Monica — forwarding CloudScale’s responses. High-level asks for you: can we accept their current mitigations for marketplace flows or do we need a gating condition (e.g., EventLytics must never receive raw email/hash unless DPA + SIEM integration)?

Specific questions to evaluate: 
- Is EU processing (eu-west-1) sufficient for our EU customer requirements, or do we need to require data residency controls in contract?

Thanks for the thread and the artifacts, Anna. I reviewed the CSV and draft contract. Quick assessment and next steps from Redwood security/compliance: 

Assessment summary:
- Region: eu-west-1 aligns with EU residency requirement for this PoC — acceptable as long as marketplace flow doesn’t egress to non-EU regions for processing. We’ll require a paragraph in the DPA confirming processing location for marketplace customers.
- Subprocessors: EventLytics must be in-scope for either SOC 2 Type II or we need documented compensating controls. MarketProxy Inc. is acceptable with contract-level restrictions on data retention and purpose limitation.
- Retention: 90 days for raw logs + longer backups is okay, but we must specify retention windows per field in the DPA (we’ll map fields from the CSV).
- Access controls: Require vendor access RBAC, MFA + IP allowlist for any accounts accessing raw events; all vendor access must be logged and retained for 12 months.

Required artifacts for our diligence (please provide these before deep-dive):
1) Subprocessor matrix (name, role, data types, SOC2? yes/no, contact) — we’ll use this to triage scope.
2) Network/data flow diagram showing tokenization/redaction points (PNG/PDF).
3) EventLytics evidence of SOC2/alternatively compensating controls documentation.
4) Redlined DPA clause proposals — add explicit residency and subprocessor constraints.

Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-matrix.xlsx, SOC2-summary.pdf (examples from our side).

Proposed calendar: Wed 26 Aug 10:00 UTC works for us. Monica will run the deep-dive and invite product/sec folks from both sides + EventLytics ops.

Marissa — can you confirm we have approval to request SOC2 copies and to push for vendor IP allowlist language as a gating item for production?

Regards,
Monica Patel
